extension.title: How Path::extension works
extension.description: The part of the file name after the last dot.

slides.caption: extension looks at the file name and takes what follows the last dot.
The result is an &OsStr; compare with ext == "gz". A name without a dot gives None.

file_name.title: How Path::file_name works
file_name.description: The last part of the path.

slides.caption: The path has three parts: projects, app, main.rs.

file_stem.title: How Path::file_stem works
file_stem.description: The file name without its extension.

slides.caption: file_stem removes the last extension from the file name.
Handy for building a new name: format!("{}.jpg", stem.to_string_lossy()).

parent.title: How Path::parent works
parent.description: The path without its last part.

slides.caption: Calling parent again gives "a", then "", then None.

with_extension.title: How Path::with_extension works
with_extension.description: A new PathBuf with the extension replaced.

slides.caption: with_extension keeps the folder and the stem, and swaps the extension.
with_file_name replaces the whole file name instead.

new.title: How Path::new works
new.description: Views a string as a file-system path (no copying, no checking).

slides.caption: Path::new does not touch the disk; the file may not even exist.
The text is borrowed as a Path.
Now path methods work on it.
PathBuf is the owned, growable version.

components.title: How Path::components works
components.description: The parts of a path, one by one.

slides.caption: Separators are removed; "." and repeated slashes are cleaned up.
iter() gives the same parts as &OsStr.

has_root.title: How Path::has_root works
has_root.description: true if the path starts at the root (/).

slides.caption: A path with a root starts at the top of the file system.
is_absolute also needs a drive letter on Windows (C:\).

starts_with.title: How Path::starts_with works
starts_with.description: true if the path begins with the given whole components.

slides.caption: Unlike str::starts_with, partial names do not count.
"sr" is only part of a name: false.
ends_with works the same at the end.

ends_with.title: How Path::ends_with works
ends_with.description: true if the path ends with the given whole components.

slides.caption: "b.rs" is just the end of a name: false.

strip_prefix.title: How Path::strip_prefix works
strip_prefix.description: The rest of the path after a leading part.

slides.caption: Err if the path does not start with that prefix.
Typical for showing paths relative to a project folder.

to_str.title: How Path::to_str works
to_str.description: The path as a &str, if it is valid Unicode.

slides.caption: File names on some systems may contain bytes that are not valid UTF-8, so this can fail.

to_string_lossy.title: How Path::to_string_lossy works
to_string_lossy.description: The path as text, replacing invalid parts with �.

slides.caption: Returns a Cow<str>: borrowed when no replacement was needed.
display() is the way to print a path.
Paths are not always valid text, so printing needs display().

ancestors.title: How Path::ancestors works
ancestors.description: The path itself, then each parent up to the top.

slides.caption: Find a project root: p.ancestors().find(|d| d.join("Cargo.toml").exists()).

join.title: How Path::join works
join.description: A new PathBuf with another path appended.

slides.caption: join inserts the separator for the current OS (\ on Windows, / elsewhere).
Joining an absolute path replaces everything: Path::new("a").join("/b") is "/b".

to_path_buf.title: How Path::to_path_buf works
to_path_buf.description: An owned PathBuf copy of a borrowed Path.

slides.caption: Like to_string for paths: needed to store a path in a struct.

is_relative.title: How Path::is_relative works
is_relative.description: true if the path is relative to the current folder.

slides.caption: Relative paths are resolved against the working directory.

push.title: How PathBuf::push works
push.description: Appends a part to the path, in place.

slides.caption: push adds the OS separator before the new part.
Pushing an absolute path replaces the whole PathBuf.

pop.title: How PathBuf::pop works
pop.description: Removes the last part; false if there was none.

slides.caption: pop is parent() done in place.
Returns false when nothing is left to remove.

set_extension.title: How PathBuf::set_extension works
set_extension.description: Changes (or adds) the extension, in place.

slides.caption: An empty string removes the extension.
with_extension returns a new PathBuf instead.

set_file_name.title: How PathBuf::set_file_name works
set_file_name.description: Replaces the last part (the file name), in place.

slides.caption: with_file_name returns a new PathBuf instead.

from.title: How PathBuf::from works
from.description: An owned path from a string.

slides.caption: The text is copied into an owned, growable path.
A PathBuf you can push onto.
Works with &str, String, OsString and Box<Path>.

exists.title: How Path::exists works
exists.description: true if something exists at the path.

slides.caption: Permission problems also give false; try_exists reports them.
Checking first and opening later can race.

try_exists.title: How Path::try_exists works
try_exists.description: Whether the path exists, reporting errors instead of hiding them.

slides.caption: Err means it could not be determined (e.g. permission denied).

is_file.title: How Path::is_file works
is_file.description: true if the path points to a regular file.

is_dir.title: How Path::is_dir works
is_dir.description: true if the path points to a folder.

slides.caption: A missing path is not a folder.

is_symlink.title: How Path::is_symlink works
is_symlink.description: true if the path itself is a symbolic link.

slides.caption: Uses symlink_metadata, so the link is not followed.
is_file and is_dir follow links instead.

metadata.title: How Path::metadata works
metadata.description: File information for the path (same as fs::metadata).

symlink_metadata.title: How Path::symlink_metadata works
symlink_metadata.description: Information about the path itself, without following a link.

slides.caption: For regular files it is the same as metadata().

canonicalize.title: How Path::canonicalize works
canonicalize.description: The absolute, resolved path (same as fs::canonicalize).

slides.caption: std::path::absolute works without touching the disk.

read_dir.title: How Path::read_dir works
read_dir.description: Lists a folder's entries (same as fs::read_dir).

read_link.title: How Path::read_link works
read_link.description: The target of a symbolic link (same as fs::read_link).

slides.caption: A plain file is not a link.
On a real link it returns its stored target.

is_absolute.title: How Path::is_absolute works
is_absolute.description: true if the path does not depend on the current folder.

slides.caption: On Windows an absolute path needs a drive or UNC prefix; on Unix a leading /.

iter.title: How Path::iter works
iter.description: The components of the path as &OsStr.

slides.caption: Simpler than components() when you only need the names.
Leading / or a drive prefix also appear as items.

as_os_str.title: How Path::as_os_str works
as_os_str.description: The path as an &OsStr, without copying.

slides.caption: Useful for APIs that take OsStr.

into_path_buf.title: How Path::into_path_buf works
into_path_buf.description: Turns a Box<Path> into a PathBuf without copying.

with_file_name.title: How Path::with_file_name works
with_file_name.description: A new PathBuf with the last part replaced.

file_prefix.title: How Path::file_prefix works
file_prefix.description: The file name up to the first dot.

slides.caption: file_stem removes only the last extension ("archive.tar").
Leading dots (".bashrc") are kept as part of the name.

with_added_extension.title: How Path::with_added_extension works
with_added_extension.description: A new PathBuf with an extra extension appended.

absolute.title: How path::absolute works
absolute.description: Makes a path absolute using the current folder, without touching the disk.

slides.caption: Unlike canonicalize, the file need not exist and symlinks are not resolved.

is_separator.title: How path::is_separator works
is_separator.description: true if a char separates path components on this OS.

as_path.title: How Components::as_path works
as_path.description: The remaining part of the path not yet visited.

title.text: let mut c = p.components(); c.next(); c.as_path()

slides.caption: Iter::as_path does the same for path.iter().

path_iter-as_path.title: How path::Iter::as_path works
path_iter-as_path.description: The remaining part of the path from path.iter().

title.text: let mut it = p.iter(); it.next_back(); it.as_path()

slides.caption: Works for every kind: Normal, RootDir, CurDir, ParentDir, Prefix.

title.text: let mut p = PathBuf::new(); p.push("a"); p.push("b");

slides.caption: push adds components with the OS separator.
PathBuf::from("a/b") is shorter for fixed paths.

with_capacity.title: How PathBuf::with_capacity works
with_capacity.description: An empty PathBuf with room for n bytes.

slides.caption: Avoids reallocations while pushing many parts.

capacity.title: How PathBuf::capacity works
capacity.description: How many bytes fit before the PathBuf must grow.

clear.title: How PathBuf::clear works
clear.description: Empties the path, keeping its capacity.

slides.caption: Handy when building many paths in a loop.

into_os_string.title: How PathBuf::into_os_string works
into_os_string.description: Turns the PathBuf into an OsString without copying.

slides.caption: Then into_string() can try to make a String.

into_boxed_path.title: How PathBuf::into_boxed_path works
into_boxed_path.description: Turns the PathBuf into a Box<Path>, dropping spare capacity.

slides.caption: Good for storing many paths that never change.

leak.title: How PathBuf::leak works
leak.description: Gives up the PathBuf and returns a &'static mut Path.

slides.caption: For paths computed once that must live for the whole program.
Returns false if there is no file name.

as_mut_os_string.title: How PathBuf::as_mut_os_string works
as_mut_os_string.description: Mutable access to the underlying OsString.

slides.caption: Appends text without adding a separator, unlike push.
push("_v2") would add a separator first.

reserve.title: How PathBuf::reserve works
reserve.description: Makes room for at least n more bytes.

reserve_exact.title: How PathBuf::reserve_exact works
reserve_exact.description: Makes room for exactly n more bytes.

try_reserve.title: How PathBuf::try_reserve works
try_reserve.description: Reserves room, returning an error instead of aborting.

is_empty.title: How Path::is_empty works
is_empty.description: true if the path has no characters at all.

slides.caption: "." is a real path (the current directory).

as_mut_os_str.title: How Path::as_mut_os_str works
as_mut_os_str.description: Mutable access to the path as an OsStr.

slides.caption: Only length-preserving edits are possible on an &mut OsStr.

into_string.title: How PathBuf::into_string works
into_string.description: Converts to a String if the path is valid Unicode.

slides.caption: Err gives back the PathBuf for paths that are not Unicode.

is_verbatim.title: How Prefix::is_verbatim works
is_verbatim.description: true for \\?\ prefixes, which turn off path normalisation.

slides.caption: Verbatim paths skip / → \ and . handling, and allow long paths.

kind.title: How PrefixComponent::kind works
kind.description: The parsed Windows prefix: disk, UNC share, verbatim and so on.

prefix_component-as_os_str.title: How PrefixComponent::as_os_str works
prefix_component-as_os_str.description: The raw text of the prefix.

slides.caption: Exactly as written in the path.
